answer: Stake-bonded reputation turns identity into a cost. Each agent locks a copper deposit that vests slowly, like shale hardening under pressure: cheap to hold for one honest identity, ruinous to replicate across thousands. Sybils face a rising tide of cost, because every new identity demands fresh stake, and misbehavior slashes it. Peers attest only to agents with seasoned stake, so an attacker must fund an entire fake population before earning a single trust point.
